transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-30 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Sara Kapoor (Apollo - Head of Data Science), Marcus Lee (Infra Lead), Dr. Nina Patel (CPO)

Auto-generated Summary: quick scoping to align on POC milestones, success metrics (latency, quality, cost), and access steps.
Topics: success criteria; workload sizing; benchmark plan; kickoff & access; mid-point review; exec readout.

00:00 Lena Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick intros then we'll jump into the timeline. Lena Park, AE at Redwood.
00:14 Sara Kapoor: hi Sara here, head of DS at Apollo. thanks, excited to scope this out.
00:20 Carlos Mendes: Carlos, I'm the SE, I'll own the benchmarks and infra touchpoints.
00:25 Marcus Lee: Marcus from infra, will handle net and security.
00:28 Dr. Nina Patel: Nina here, product—looking for clear success on clinical summarization accuracy and speed.

01:02 Lena Park: goal for today is to land on a 4-week POC timeline, define success criteria, what data you can give us, and next steps. does that sound right?
01:12 Sara Kapoor: yep that's perfect. our timeline is fairly aggressive, we want an exec readout early May if possible.

02:05 Carlos Mendes: first, success criteria. from what we heard: quality of summaries (we can use ROUGE or QA-based F1 on a labeled set), latency SLO 95th pctl < 250ms for single-document retrieval+generate flows, and cost target roughly <$0.10 per processed document in production equivalent. does that match?
02:28 Sara Kapoor: latency ideally under 200ms but we'll compromise to 250ms if cost tradeoff is better. quality is non-negotiable though — we need medical factuality at or above our current baseline.
02:40 Dr. Nina Patel: also auditability — we need traceable logs and the ability to prove no PHI leakage.

04:10 Carlos Mendes: noted. on workload sizing, can you give a sense of average document length and concurrency?
04:20 Sara Kapoor: avg doc is about 1,200 words (~800-1,000 tokens), peak concurrency about 15-20 qps for batch reporting, but user-facing flows are 2-5 qps.
04:35 Marcus Lee: we will likely route user-facing to low-latency path. our acceptance test should simulate 20 qps sustained for 10 minutes.

06:00 Lena Park: benchmark plan we suggest: baseline hosted Redwood model run on a sample set (1k queries), record p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec throughput, and output quality metrics. then repeat on a dedicated node with quantization profile to compare cost/latency.
06:22 Carlos Mendes: SE note — we'll run 3 runs: cold cache, warmed KV cache, and warmed with batching to see differences. we'll capture token counts and per-invocation cost estimate.

08:10 Sara Kapoor: for quality, we can provide 200 labeled QA pairs for human eval scoring. is that enough?
08:18 Carlos Mendes: yes that will be fine for the POC. we'll also do automated overlap metrics.

10:05 Marcus Lee: security — we require VPC peering or private link, our KMS for encryption, SSO via SAML/Okta, and SOC2 documents. how does Redwood support these?
10:20 Lena Park: we support VPC peering and private deployments; we'll share the security pack and a SAML guide. Redwood can integrate with customer KMS for key management and we provide audit logs.
10:38 Marcus Lee: timeline for network setup — we can open a 2 hour window w/c 2026-04-06 for peering work.

12:00 Carlos Mendes: timeline/milestones proposal: Week 0 (kickoff) — 2026-04-07: confirm scope, transfer sample data; Week 1 — access setup & ingestion; Week 2 — baseline runs & initial quality eval; Week 3 — perf tuning and mid-point review with results; Week 4 — final runs, runbook and exec readout prep; Exec readout target week of 2026-05-04.

14:22 Sara Kapoor: that sequence works. we may need an extra day for legal to sign the data processing addendum but try to keep the kickoff week.

16:10 Carlos Mendes: specifics on benchmarks: we'll run 1k synthetic queries plus your 200 labeled QA for quality. measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tail latency under mixed load, throughput with batching disabled and enabled, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll also verify KV cache hit rates.

18:40 Dr. Nina Patel: on success criteria for acceptance — quality threshold: F1 >= 0.82 on our labeled set, p95 latency <= 250ms for user flows, and cost projection below your target. if any of those fail we iterate but need to understand remediation path.

21:15 Lena Park: agreed — acceptance gates: 1) quality check, 2) latency SLO, 3) security checklist signed off. mid-point review will highlight remediation plan.

23:30 Marcus Lee: practically for infra we need ingredient list: IP ranges, desired ports, and a bastion for initial debugging. Carlos can you produce a minimal connectivity doc?
23:45 Carlos Mendes: yes I'll send a short network checklist and a step-by-step for peering.

26:00 Sara Kapoor: data — we can provide 50 de-identified notes for initial ingestion and 200 labeled QA pairs. full 1k synthetic queries we expect Redwood to generate to stress.

28:20 Carlos Mendes: ingestion — we'll provide an ingestion script and a CSV template; sample mapping fields like patient_id (masked), note_text, encounter_date. please keep PHI out.

30:05 Lena Park: risk discussion — primary risks are data access delay (legal), network setup, and model quality gaps. mitigation: start legal DPA review immediately, schedule network window early, and plan a rapid iterate cycle after mid-point review.

33:40 Dr. Nina Patel: about dedicated vs hosted — if hosted meets latency and cost we prefer it for speed, but if not we'll consider Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput.

35:00 Carlos Mendes: we'll include both hosted baseline and dedicated config in the benchmark doc so you can see tradeoffs.

37:12 Marcus Lee: any concerns about data residency? we must keep data in us-east-1.
37:20 Lena Park: yes we can pin region for the POC; we'll note that in the setup guide.

40:00 Sara Kapoor: ok so what's the kickoff date proposed? 2026-04-07?
40:05 Lena Park: yes propose 2026-04-07 for kickoff. Carlos and Marcus will coordinate the access window earlier if possible the week prior.

42:30 Carlos Mendes: deliverables timeline recap: by 2026-03-31 Lena will send POC deck + pricing; Carlos will send benchmark plan by 2026-04-03; customer provides sample data by 2026-04-02; network peering window the week of 2026-04-06.

45:10 Sara Kapoor: sounds good. can you also include cost projections for a 3 month run rate?
45:20 Lena Park: yes we'll add a short cost projection doc and show hosted vs dedicated ballparks.

47:50 Dr. Nina Patel: final question — can Redwood provide a HIPAA BAA?
47:58 Lena Park: we do; our legal team can start the BAA and DPA process. I'll loop them in after this call.

50:00 Lena Park: ok recap and next steps: I will send the POC scope deck and pricing today, Carlos will send benchmark plan, Marcus will schedule peering window, Sara to share sample de-id data. target kickoff 2026-04-07, mid-point review mid-PoC (week of 2026-04-20), exec readout week of 2026-05-04.
50:35 Sara Kapoor: thanks everyone, we'll aim to meet these dates.
50:42 Marcus Lee: thanks all.
50:46 Dr. Nina Patel: thanks.
51:00 Lena Park: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs. bye.
51:12 end
